* Assemble the command and hand it to the user instead of running it - inside the claudex sandbox `colab` aborts at startup because it cannot open `~/.config/colab-cli/colab.log`, and the `rclone` behind `--input` cannot read `~/.config/rclone/rclone.conf`
* Have it run from the directory of the project the command belongs to, calling the script by its path since `bin/` is not on `PATH` - only what `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` lists there reaches the runtime, so a gitignored model or dataset needs `--input` and the variables `.env` sets never arrive

## Command

```bash
cd {project}
"$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/bin/colabofy.sh" --gpu L4 --input ~/.cache/{project} --output {directory} -- uv run python {script}.py
```

Pass whatever `.env` would have supplied as a prefix to COMMAND (`env DEVICE=cuda uv run ...`), leaving out `HTTP_PROXY` and the rest that point at this machine.
Check that the `.python-version` `.claude/rules/pyproject.md` requires is in place before handing it over, since that rule records the build failure on Colab without one.
